---
title: "Physical Authority and Reusable Composition"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## CONVERGING concept

This page explains the current candidate design. It does not define API,
physics, validation, or failure behavior; the linked contracts remain the sole
authority.
:::

## Design pressure

A reusable circuit model needs to expose a stable useful surface while its
author can improve its internal expansion. At the same time, every consumer,
compiler, diagram, and backend must refer to one physical circuit rather than
to several nearly equivalent descriptions.

## CircuitPlan is the physical authority {#plan-as-physical-authority}

SCNSim gives a `CircuitPlan` sole physical authority. Immutable component
catalogs provide instances with attributable source identity.

## CompositePlan is the reuse boundary {#composite-as-reuse-boundary}

A Composite is one component that deliberately publishes only the pins,
parameters, and observation coordinates intended for its consumer. Its
children are expansion evidence, not automatically public circuit API.

This makes composition a boundary, not a shorthand for leaking a component's
internal topology. A diagram or compiled expansion can explain that authority,
but neither becomes another circuit definition.

## Problem solved

The boundary lets a model author reuse a Composite without forcing every
Notebook to know its child IDs, wiring, or calibration fan-out. It also means a
consumer can identify the exact component source and physical Plan behind an
analysis, even when the model is assembled from built-in and custom catalogs.

## Intentionally not owned

This concept does not choose optimizer bounds, Design Targets, runtime
requests, or results. It also does not turn a Composite into a mutable global
catalog, expose hidden children by inference, or make a schematic a competing
physical authority.
